title: Tenant-centric SLO Gate with Safe Fail-safing and Graduated Load Shedding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a tenant-centric SLO gate that combines per-tenant, per-dependency, and per-model trip thresholds with graduated load-shedding and safe fallback routing. Goal is to give platform teams deterministic, observable control over when we soft-trip traffic for a tenant and how to fall back to safe alternatives (cached responses, downgraded model variants, region failover) without violating downstream SLAs or introducing data leakage. This ticket covers: trip/window algorithms, hysteresis, safe fallback behaviors, rollout plan, metrics/alerting, and a short runbook for on-call. The implementation must be pluggable in the serving runtime and configurable from Console (policy + thresholds).
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant SLO policy objects can be defined via Console and returned through the policy API
Circuit evaluates per-tenant metrics in 60s sliding windows with configurable decay and can soft-trip (probabilistic shedding) and hard-trip (denylist) separately
On soft-trip: traffic is gradually shed according to configured percentages and guided to safe fallbacks: prefix-kv cache, smaller/quantized model variants, or queued retry with capped latency
On hard-trip: new requests receive a clear fallback path (cached/alternative model) and circuit state transitions are logged and visible in Console with trace links
Multi-region failover integration exists: if primary region cross-tenant capacity breach occurs, policy can route affected tenants to secondary region preserving tenancy isolation
Observability: dashboards show per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, trip probability, and fallback counts; alerts fire when a tenant's soft-trip rate exceeds configured threshold
Automated canary rollout: feature flag + canary exposes the policy to a small tenant cohort with metrics recording before wider rollout
E2E tests: synthetic load harness that asserts correct shedding percentages and fallbacks under controlled latency and error patterns
tasks: Design policy schema for per-tenant SLO gates and fallback graphs (Arjun)
Implement streaming window evaluator with exponential decay and configurable hysteresis (runtime team)
Add fallback executors: kv-cache fallback, model-variant reroute, queued-retry with max-wait (runtime)
Console UI: policy editor and per-tenant simulator + rollout control (Product + Console)
Instrument metrics and traces: trip events, decision reasons, fallback resolution (Observability)
Create canary plan and runbook, include safe rollback and drill steps (SRE)
Add e2e and unit tests covering soft-trip probabilistic shedding and hard-trip deterministic denial
comments: 2025-02-10 Maya Chen: Kickoff — scoped to tenant-level gates, we will not change default global breaker behavior in this ticket. Focus is policy API + runtime evaluator + fallbacks. 2-week cadence for MVP.

2025-02-11 Arjun Patel: Prototype of decay-window evaluator complete. Using a 60s sliding window with alpha=0.2 for decay gave stable responsiveness in local load tests. Will open PR against runtime-inference next.

2025-02-13 Sophie Laurent (Design): Console mockups uploaded to Drive and linked below. UI includes a simulator where you can inject p95 and error rates to preview trip probability and fallback counts.

2025-02-14 Diego Rivera (SRE): Suggested safe-fallback order: 1) prefix KV cache 2) cached embeddings 3) quantized small model variant (lower capacity) 4) region failover 5) graceful rejection with Retry-After header. Avoid automated long queues that block ingress permanently.
2025-02-16 Arjun Patel: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1187 — implements evaluator and exposes trip telemetry. Requesting initial review from @sre-team and @obs-team.
2025-02-17 Observability: Dashboard draft available at https://grafana.redwood/s/dTenantSLOs — includes per-tenant trip rate, p95 latency, fallback counts. Need feedback on cardinality concerns.

2025-02-18 Maya Chen: Decision — implement two-level trips: soft-trip (probabilistic shedding, configurable percent) and hard-trip (binary denylist). Soft-trip will include an exponential warmup/decay to avoid oscillation. Proceeding to implementation phase.
2025-02-18 Arjun Patel: Blocking: we need a small feature flag infra change to store policy toggles at tenant granularity (ENG-47899). I've added it to dependencies.
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Chose hybrid windowing (sliding window with decay) after microbench tests vs fixed-bucket windows — better responsiveness to spikes
2025-02-15: Agreed to soft-trip by probabilistic shedding to avoid broad user-visible 503s and to allow some success rate for continued feedback collection
2025-02-18: Multi-region failover remains opt-in per-tenant; hygiene checks required to prevent cross-region data residency violations
notes: Operational constraints: keep per-tenant metrics cardinality bounded — only surface top N tenants and sampling for low-traffic tenants
Security: fallback to alternative models must preserve tenant isolation; no cross-tenant model sharing unless model is marked multi-tenant-safe
Rollout: start with internal tenants and low-risk customers; monitor fallback-rates and SLO drift closely and be ready to rollback via FF
Perf target: evaluator adds <2ms p95 to request path when cache hit; off-path decisions should be async where possible
